Class ParsleyOwnOutputInterceptor

java.lang.Object
io.github.tobyjamesclements.parsley.ParsleyOwnOutputInterceptor
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable, org.apache.kafka.clients.producer.ProducerInterceptor<Object,Object>, org.apache.kafka.common.Configurable
public final class ParsleyOwnOutputInterceptor extends Object implements org.apache.kafka.clients.producer.ProducerInterceptor<Object,Object>
The producer-side half of the ownOutputs clock: it publishes every acknowledged send to a declared sink topic into this instance's ParsleyOwnOutputRegistry, from which the stream threads fold the coordinates into each outbound stamp.

Not public API. This class is public only because Kafka instantiates producer interceptors reflectively; CausalStreams injects it into every stream producer through the producer.interceptor.classes config. Do not configure it by hand: without the registry id CausalStreams co-injects (ParsleyOwnOutputRegistry.CONFIG_KEY) every callback is a no-op.

    • onAcknowledgement

      public void onAcknowledgement(@Nullable org.apache.kafka.clients.producer.RecordMetadata metadata, @Nullable Exception exception)
      Resolves a tracked send: folds a successful ack's committed coordinate into the registry's per-coordinate max, then clears its pending count (T2.1 — exactly one callback per send, abort included, failures carrying a non-null exception). Runs on the producer network thread; everything it touches is the registry's concurrent state. A null metadata (no coordinate to resolve) is counted as a failure so a crossing wait releases loudly rather than hanging on a send that will never resolve.

      Fold-before-acknowledge is load-bearing: tracker.acknowledged wakes any crossing-wait waiter, whose very next step is draining the registry into the ownOutputs clock and stamping. Folding after the wake-up opens a window where the released stamp misses exactly the coordinate whose ack released it — an under-claiming stamp, the crossing wait's whole reason to exist (found live in CausalFanOutScopedFrontierIT). The acked map is a ConcurrentHashMap written before the tracker's monitor notification, so the woken waiter always observes the fold.

      Specified by:
      onAcknowledgement in interface org.apache.kafka.clients.producer.ProducerInterceptor<Object,Object>
